text:
Maya (Support): heads up — large customer (ACME) opened a critical ticket: multiple requests returning 5xx and timeouts starting ~11:58 UTC during their billing window. they sent logs and screenshots.
Alex (Oncall): joining. can you paste the sample request + error?
Maya (Support): pasted from the ticket: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
x-customer-id: acme
Body: {prompt: "…"}
Response: 502 Bad Gateway, sometimes 504 after 30s
Trace: gateway->hosted-inference-1 -> runtime-3 : upstream reset
```
Maya (Support): they said it was intermittent (10-30% of calls) and latency for others jumped from ~200ms to 1.5s.
Alex (Oncall): Priya, can you check gateway and autoscaler metrics for the eu-west region around 11:50-12:10?
Priya (SRE): looking — gateway error rate spike correlated with a burst of short seq requests. I see queue depth on hosted-inference-1 increase, and a backlog on the runtime service. CPU on runtime pods hit ~92% for the model-serving container.
Jin (Infra): any deploys around that time? opsbot?
OpsBot: deploys: no prod deploys in eu-west between 11:30 and 12:30 UTC.
Liz (ML): which model were they hitting? large-model-v2? quantized?
Maya (Support): customer included model: gptq-13b-q4. They said they pin to that model.
Priya (SRE): ok that model has higher per-token CPU during decoding. I'm seeing an increased kernel time for attention ops in runtime-3. Also noticed KV cache miss burst — a lot of unique prefixes during billing notifications.
Alex (Oncall): quick mitigation options? fallback route to a cheaper variant? throttle?
Jin (Infra): we can enable the route fallback to gptq-6b-compat for that customer — we've done that before. also can temporarily increase replicas in the dedicated pool for hosted-inference-1.
Liz (ML): gptq-6b-compat has lower memory and token throughput variance, should cut CPU per token ~40%. Quality might be slightly lower for long-context billing text, but acceptable as a short-term mitigation.
Priya (SRE): doing two things now: 1) increase pool replicas by +3 (scaling action) 2) add a per-customer routing override to route acme -> gptq-6b-compat with circuit breaker after 10s. applying changes, will monitor.
Priya (SRE): scaling policy change applied. replicas warmed up in ~45s. fallbacks enabled.
Maya (Support): updated customer: told them we're rolling a mitigation and will monitor, asked for any reproducible example. they appreciated the quick update. :thumbsup:
Alex (Oncall): monitoring dashboards — error rate dropped to baseline within 2 minutes after fallback. latency for routed requests stable ~220ms. however some already-in-flight requests still 504.
Priya (SRE): confirm: gateway 5xx reduced from 18% -> 1.5% in the window. CPU normalized to 60-70% after scale.
Jin (Infra): note: autoscaler didn't react fast enough because the burst was ~30s and the policy cooldown is 2m. we should consider a burst capacity buffer for billing windows.
Liz (ML): also flagging model quantization profile: gptq-13b-q4 has occasional kernel hotpaths that amplify under many short requests (small seq). we should investigate compilation flags that better support short-sequence throughput.
Maya (Support): customer wants a postmortem and action plan. ticket linked: #T-4821.
Alex (Oncall): immediate action items (short):
- Priya: propose and deploy a short-burst autoscaler policy for hosted-inference pools (target: handle +200% QPS spikes for 45s) — due EOD
- Jin: add a per-customer routing knob that can be toggled from support console without infra intervention — P0-ish
- Liz: run perf regression and kernel trace for gptq-13b-q4 on short sequences; propose compilation/tuning change — due 3 business days
- Maya: follow up with ACME, send RCA draft and ask for reproducible logs — today
Alex (Oncall): longer-term: explore prefix caching improvements and smarter request coalescing for billing-notification patterns. add to roadmap.
Priya (SRE): creating incident ticket and will kick off a short war room postmortem at 15:00 UTC. I'll attach metrics, flamegraphs, and the command we used to reproduce.
Maya (Support): ACME provided a small repro curl that recreates the 502 ~30% of the time: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'x-customer-id: acme' -d '{"prompt":"billing ping","max_tokens":20}' -v
```
Liz (ML): I'll try running that against a local runtime with profiler. can we get a staging snapshot of their traffic pattern?
Priya (SRE): yes — exporting sample traces to /incidents/1764209876/export-1.log.
Jin (Infra): tagging this for oncall-runbook: "billing-window spike" and adding a playbook: immediate-scale + route-fallback + notify-support.
Alex (Oncall): good. once Priya creates the postmortem doc, we'll do an internal review and then send ACME the RCA and timeline. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
OpsBot: incident created: INC-2026-115 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-115)
Priya (SRE): postmortem checklist note: measure customer impact (requests failed, perceived latency), root cause hypothesis (model CPU hotpath + autoscaler cooldown + high unique prefixes), remediation (short-burst scaler, route knob, quant tuning), timeline, and owners.
Maya (Support): ACME replied: "thanks — we'll accept fallback for now; please keep us posted."
Alex (Oncall): closing this slack thread once postmortem doc is created. will include action-item tracker.
Priya (SRE): last note — recommend a follow-up with product to discuss offering a "billing window SLA" option (reserved burst capacity) for customers with predictable spikes.
Maya (Support): adding that to the customer feature request queue.
Alex (Oncall): end of thread — monitoring continues.
